NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager whose new melons all failed, against everyone's advice, says it was still their choice to try.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: A month ago, against the advice of almost everybody, (name1) planted (his/her) whole garden with a new kind of melon nobody on Isola had grown before. The melons didn't grow. Not one. The garden is just a patch of bare, sad earth with a few vines lying in it. Today someone at the fire starts to say, "Well, if you'd listened..." and (name1) holds up a hand, not unkindly. "I know," (he/she) says. "Everyone said it might not work. They were right that it might not. It was still my choice, and I'd make it again. I wanted to try." There is a pause. Then somebody passes (him/her) a piece of fish, and the talk moves on to other things. Next season (name1) plants beans like everybody else, and three melon seeds in a corner, just in case. One of them comes up. Just one. (He/she) is unreasonably proud of it.
